title.en: Volume 87 Biographies 12: Xiao, Fu, Shen, Li, Liang
title.raw: 卷八十七 列傳第十二 蕭輔沈李梁 Volume 87 Biographies 12: Xiao, Fu, Shen, Li, Liang

sentences.zh: 25%蕭銑蕭銑，後梁宣帝曾孫也。

translations.literal: Biography of Xiao Xian: Xiao Xian was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Xuan of the Later Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Xiao Xian. Xiao Xian was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Xuan of the Later Liang.

sentences.zh: 祖巖，開皇初叛隋降陳，陳亡，文帝誅之。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan, in the early Kaihuang era rebelled against Sui and submitted to Chen; when Chen perished, Emperor Wen executed him.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan, in the early Kaihuang reign, rebelled against Sui and went over to Chen; when Chen fell, Emperor Wen of Sui had him put to death.

sentences.zh: 銑少貧，傭書，事母孝。

translations.literal: Xian in youth was poor, hired out as a copyist, and served his mother filially.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Xian was poor and made his living copying books; he was devoted in caring for his mother.

sentences.zh: 煬帝以外戚擢為羅川令。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang, on account of maternal kinship, promoted him to magistrate of Luochuan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang promoted him to magistrate of Luochuan because of his connection as an imperial in-law.

sentences.zh: 大業十三年，岳州校尉董景珍、雷世猛，旅帥鄭文秀、許玄徹、萬瓚、徐德基、郭華，沔人張繡等謀反隋，且推景珍為主，景珍曰：「吾素微，雖假名號，眾不厭。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Daye, the Yuezhou adjutant Dong Jingzhen and Lei Shimeng, the itinerant commanders Zheng Wenxiu, Xu Xuanche, Wan Zan, Xu Deji, and Guo Hua, Zhang Xiu of Mian and others plotted to rebel against Sui and wished to install Jingzhen as leader. Jingzhen said: "I have always been obscure; even if I borrow a title, the masses will not be satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Daye, the Yuezhou adjutant Dong Jingzhen and Lei Shimeng, together with the itinerant commanders Zheng Wenxiu, Xu Xuanche, Wan Zan, Xu Deji, Guo Hua, Zhang Xiu of Mian, and others, plotted to rebel against Sui and meant to set up Jingzhen as their leader. Jingzhen said, "I have always been insignificant; even if we borrow a title for me, the people will not be content.

sentences.zh: 羅川令，故梁裔也，寬仁大度，有武皇遺風。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Luochuan is a descendant of the former Liang, magnanimous and tolerant, with the lingering manner of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Luochuan is a descendant of the old Liang, broad-minded and generous, and still carries something of Emperor Wu's bearing.

sentences.zh: 且吾聞帝王之興，必有符命。

translations.literal: Moreover I have heard that the rise of emperors must have a mandate sign.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, I have heard that when emperors arise, there is always a token of Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 隋冠帶悉號『起梁』，蕭氏中興象也。

translations.literal: All Sui caps and belts are labeled 'Qi Liang'—an image of the Xiao clan's restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Every Sui official's cap and belt is marked 'Rise of Liang'—a sign that the house of Xiao will rise again.

sentences.zh: 今推之，以應天順人，不亦可乎？」

translations.literal: Now if we advance him, to accord with Heaven and follow the people—is that not fitting?"
translations.idiomatic: If we now set him at the head, to answer Heaven and win the people—would that not be right?"

sentences.zh: 乃遣人告銑。

translations.literal: Thereupon they sent a man to inform Xian.
translations.idiomatic: With that they sent someone to tell Xian.

sentences.zh: 銑即報景珍書曰：「我先君昔事隋，職貢無廢，乃貪我土宇，滅我宗祊，我是以痛心疾首，恫心疾首，思刷厥恥。

translations.literal: Xian at once replied to Jingzhen in a letter: "My late forebear formerly served Sui, tribute never ceased, yet they coveted our territory and extinguished our ancestral temple—I therefore am heart-stricken and grieved in heart, thinking to wipe away that shame.
translations.idiomatic: Xian at once wrote back to Jingzhen: "My forefathers once served Sui and never failed in tribute, yet Sui coveted our lands and destroyed our ancestral temple. That is why I am heartbroken and sick with grief, determined to wash away that disgrace.

sentences.zh: 傑今天誘乃衷，公等降心，將大復梁緒，僥福於先帝，吾敢不糾厲士眾以從公哉！」

translations.literal: Fortuitously today Heaven guides our hearts; you and others lower your hearts—we shall greatly restore Liang's line, trusting in fortune from the former emperor; how dare I not muster warriors to follow you!"
translations.idiomatic: Now Heaven has turned our hearts toward this day, and you have bent your will to the cause—we shall restore the line of Liang and may yet share in my forefather's blessing. How could I refuse to rally soldiers and follow you!"

sentences.zh: 即募兵數千，揚言跡盜，將以應景珍。

translations.literal: Immediately he recruited several thousand troops, announcing he would pursue bandits, intending to respond to Jingzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately raised several thousand men, claiming he would hunt down bandits, and prepared to join Jingzhen.

sentences.zh: 會潁川賊沈柳生寇縣，銑出戰不利，謂其下曰：「岳陽豪傑將推我為主，今天下叛隋，吾能守節獨完哉？

translations.literal: It happened that the Yingchuan bandit Shen Liusheng raided the county; Xian went out to fight without success and said to his followers: "The Yueyang heroes will advance me as leader; now the realm rebels against Sui—can I alone keep integrity intact?
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Yingchuan bandit Shen Liusheng raided the county. Xian went out to fight and was beaten. He told his men, "The heroes of Yueyang mean to make me their leader. The empire is in revolt against Sui—how can I alone cling to loyalty and stay whole?

sentences.zh: 且吾先人國於此，若徇其請復梁祚，因以半紙檄召群盜，誰敢不從？」

translations.literal: Moreover our forebears established a state here; if I follow their request to restore Liang's fate, then with half a sheet of proclamation summon the bandits—who would dare not follow?"
translations.idiomatic: Our ancestors once had a kingdom here. If I accept their plea and restore the house of Liang, a half-sheet of proclamation will summon every outlaw in the land—who would dare refuse?"

sentences.zh: 眾悅。

translations.literal: The crowd was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The men were delighted.

sentences.zh: 乃以十月稱梁公，旗幟服色悉用其舊。

translations.literal: Thereupon in the tenth month he styled himself Duke of Liang; banners and regalia all used the old forms.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he took the title Duke of Liang; flags, standards, and dress all followed the old Liang style.

sentences.zh: 柳生以眾歸銑，用為車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Liusheng with his forces submitted to Xian, who appointed him Grand General of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Liusheng brought his troops over to Xian, who made him Grand General of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 不五日，遠近爭附，眾數萬，乃趨巴陵。

translations.literal: Within less than five days, far and near competed to attach themselves; the host numbered tens of thousands, and he hastened to Baling.
translations.idiomatic: In fewer than five days men from near and far flocked to him until his force numbered in the tens of thousands, and he marched on Baling.

sentences.zh: 景珍遣徐德基、郭華率強姓百迎謁，而先見柳生。

translations.literal: Jingzhen sent Xu Deji and Guo Hua leading a hundred of the powerful surnames to greet him, but they first met Liusheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen sent Xu Deji and Guo Hua with a hundred leading clansmen to welcome him, but they met Liusheng first.

sentences.zh: 柳生與其下謀曰：「梁公起，我最先附，勛第一。

translations.literal: Liusheng plotted with his followers, saying: "When the Duke of Liang rose, I was the first to attach myself—merit first.
translations.idiomatic: Liusheng plotted with his men and said, "When the Duke of Liang rose, I was the first to join him—my merit comes first.

sentences.zh: 今岳陽兵眾而位多，誰肯為我下？

translations.literal: Now the Yueyang troops are many and positions many—who would be willing to be beneath me?
translations.idiomatic: Now the army at Yueyang is large and there are many high posts—who will willingly rank below me?

sentences.zh: 不如殺德基，質其人，獨挾梁主以進，則吾誰先？」

translations.literal: Better kill Deji, hold their people hostage, and alone lead the Lord of Liang forward—then who would get ahead of me?
translations.idiomatic: Better kill Deji, take his men hostage, and march forward alone with the Lord of Liang—then who could get ahead of me?

sentences.zh: 因殺德基，詣中軍白銑。

translations.literal: Thereupon he killed Deji and went to the central army to report to Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He killed Deji and went to the main camp to tell Xian.

sentences.zh: 銑驚曰：「今欲撥亂，遽自相屠，我不能為若主矣！」

translations.literal: Xian startled said: "Now we wish to settle chaos, yet suddenly butcher one another—I cannot be your lord!
translations.idiomatic: Xian was shocked and said, "We mean to put down disorder, yet you butcher one another at once—I cannot be your leader!

sentences.zh: 步出軍門。

translations.literal: He walked out of the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: He walked out of the camp gate.

sentences.zh: 柳生懼，伏地請罪。

translations.literal: Liusheng in fear prostrated himself begging pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Liusheng threw himself on the ground and begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 銑責宥之，陳兵而進。

translations.literal: Xian reproved but forgave him, arrayed troops and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Xian rebuked him but spared him, then drew up his army and marched on.

sentences.zh: 景珍曰：「德其倡義竭誠，柳生擅殺之，不誅，無以為政。

translations.literal: Jingzhen said: "De he who launched the cause with utmost sincerity; Liusheng killed him on his own authority—if not executed, there can be no government.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen said, "Deji was the one who launched this cause with all his heart. Liusheng murdered him on his own—if he is not punished, there can be no rule.

sentences.zh: 且兇賊與共處，必為亂。」

translations.literal: Moreover to dwell with violent bandits—they will surely make chaos."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, if we keep violent men among us, they will surely bring ruin."

sentences.zh: 銑因斬柳生。

translations.literal: Xian thereupon beheaded Liusheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xian then had Liusheng beheaded.

sentences.zh: 於是築壇城南，柴上帝，自稱梁王。

translations.literal: Thereupon he built an altar south of the city, sacrificed to the Supreme Emperor, and styled himself King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He built an altar south of the city, offered sacrifice to the Supreme Lord, and declared himself King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 有異鳥至，建元為鳳鳴。

translations.literal: A strange bird arrived; he established an era name Fengming (Phoenix Cry).
translations.idiomatic: A strange bird appeared, and he took the era name Fengming, "Phoenix Cry."

sentences.zh: 義寧二年，僭稱皇帝，署百官，一用梁故事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yining, he presumptuously styled himself emperor, appointed officials of all ranks, all following Liang precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yining he declared himself emperor, appointed officials at every level, and followed Liang institutions throughout.

sentences.zh: 追謚從父琮為孝靖帝，祖巖河間忠烈王，父璿文憲王。

translations.literal: He posthumously ennobled his father's cousin Cong as Emperor Xiaojing, grandfather Yan as Prince Zhonglie of Hejian, father Xuan as Prince Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: He gave posthumous titles to his father's cousin Cong as Emperor Xiaojing, his grandfather Yan as Prince Zhonglie of Hejian, and his father Xuan as Prince Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 封景珍晉王，雷世猛秦王，鄭文秀楚王，許玄徹燕王，萬瓚魯王，張繡齊王，楊道生宋王。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Jingzhen as Prince of Jin, Lei Shimeng as Prince of Qin, Zheng Wenxiu as Prince of Chu, Xu Xuanche as Prince of Yan, Wan Zan as Prince of Lu, Zhang Xiu as Prince of Qi, Yang Daosheng as Prince of Song.
translations.idiomatic: He made Jingzhen Prince of Jin, Lei Shimeng Prince of Qin, Zheng Wenxiu Prince of Chu, Xu Xuanche Prince of Yan, Wan Zan Prince of Lu, Zhang Xiu Prince of Qi, and Yang Daosheng Prince of Song.

sentences.zh: 隋將張鎮州、王仁壽擊銑，不能克，及隋亡，乃與寧長真等率嶺南州縣降於銑。

translations.literal: The Sui generals Zhang Zhenzhou and Wang Renshou attacked Xian but could not overcome him; when Sui perished, they with Ning Changzhen and others led the Lingnan prefectures and counties to submit to Xian.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui generals Zhang Zhenzhou and Wang Renshou attacked Xian but could not defeat him. After Sui fell, they and Ning Changzhen and others led the prefectures and counties of Lingnan in submission to him.

sentences.zh: 時林士弘據江南，銑遣將蘇胡兒拔豫章，使楊道生取南郡，張繡略定嶺表。

translations.literal: At that time Lin Shihong held the Jiangnan region; Xian sent the general Su Hu'er to take Yuzhang, sent Yang Daosheng to take Nan commandery, and Zhang Xiu to pacify the Lingnan region.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Shihong then held the lower Yangtze. Xian sent Su Hu'er to seize Yuzhang, Yang Daosheng to take Nan commandery, and Zhang Xiu to bring the far south under control.

sentences.zh: 西至三峽，南交趾，北距漢水，皆附屬，勝兵四十萬。

translations.literal: West to the Three Gorges, south to Jiaozhi, north to the Han River—all attached themselves; battle-ready troops four hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: From the Three Gorges in the west to Jiaozhi in the south and the Han River in the north, all submitted to him; his field army reached four hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，徙都江陵，復園廟。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude, he moved the capital to Jiangling and restored the imperial clan temples.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude he moved his capital to Jiangling and restored the ancestral temples of the house of Liang.

sentences.zh: 引岑文本為中書侍郎，掌機密。

translations.literal: He brought in Cen Wende as Vice Director of the Secretariat, in charge of secrets.
translations.idiomatic: He brought in Cen Wende as Vice Director of the Secretariat to handle confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 遣道生攻峽州，刺史許紹擊破之，士死過半。

translations.literal: He sent Daosheng to attack Xiazhou; the prefect Xu Shao defeated him and more than half the soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Daosheng against Xiazhou, but the prefect Xu Shao routed him and more than half his men were killed.

sentences.zh: 三年，高祖詔夔州總管趙郡王孝恭討之，拔通、開二州，斬偽東平王阇提。

translations.literal: In the third year, Emperor Gaozu ordered the Commandery Prince of Zhao, General-in-Chief of Kuizhou Xiaogong, to campaign against him; he took the two prefectures Tong and Kai and beheaded the false Prince of Dongping Zheti.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Emperor Gaozu ordered the Prince of Zhao, General-in-Chief of Kuizhou Li Xiaogong, to attack him. Xiaogong took Tong and Kai prefectures and beheaded the false Prince of Dongping, Zheti.

sentences.zh: 諸將擅兵橫恣，銑恐浸不制，乃陽議休兵營農，以黜其權。

translations.literal: The generals arrogantly wielded troops and acted willfully; Xian feared they would gradually be uncontrollable, and thus openly discussed resting troops and farming to strip their power.
translations.idiomatic: His generals abused their armies and acted as they pleased. Xian feared he would lose control of them, so he openly proposed standing the troops down for farming in order to curb their power.

sentences.zh: 大司馬董景珍之弟為將軍，怨之，謀作亂，事泄，被誅。

translations.literal: The younger brother of the Grand Marshal Dong Jingzhen was a general, resentful of this, and plotted rebellion; when the affair leaked he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The younger brother of Grand Marshal Dong Jingzhen, who was himself a general, resented this and plotted a revolt. When the plot was exposed, he was executed.

sentences.zh: 景珍方鎮長沙，銑下書赦之，召還江陵。

translations.literal: Jingzhen was then garrisoning Changsha; Xian sent an edict pardoning him and summoned him back to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen was then holding Changsha. Xian issued a pardon and summoned him back to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 景珍懼，遣使詣孝恭，舉地降。

translations.literal: Jingzhen feared, sent envoys to Xiaogong, and surrendered his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen was afraid, sent envoys to Xiaogong, and surrendered his territory.

sentences.zh: 銑遣張繡攻景珍，景珍曰：「前年醢彭越，往年殺韓信，獨不見乎！

translations.literal: Xian sent Zhang Xiu to attack Jingzhen. Jingzhen said: "In former years Peng Yue was minced, in past years Han Xin was killed—have you alone not seen it!
translations.idiomatic: Xian sent Zhang Xiu to attack Jingzhen. Jingzhen said, "Years ago Peng Yue was boiled alive; not long ago Han Xin was killed—have you alone never heard of it?

sentences.zh: 奈何相攻？」

translations.literal: Why attack each other?"
translations.idiomatic: Why turn on each other now?"

sentences.zh: 繡不答，圍之。

translations.literal: Xiu did not answer and besieged him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu made no reply and laid siege to him.

sentences.zh: 景珍潰而走，麾下殺之。

translations.literal: Jingzhen was routed and fled; his subordinates killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen was broken and fled, but his own men killed him.

sentences.zh: 銑進繡為尚書令。

translations.literal: Xian advanced Xiu to Imperial Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: Xian promoted Zhang Xiu to Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 繡恃功，亦驕蹇，銑又誅之。

translations.literal: Xiu relying on merit was also arrogant; Xian again executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu, trusting in his achievements, grew insolent as well, and Xian had him executed too.

sentences.zh: 銑性外寬內忌，疾勝己者，於是大臣舊將皆疑間，多叛去，銑不能禁，由此愈弱。

translations.literal: Xian by nature was outwardly lenient and inwardly jealous, hating those who surpassed himself; thereupon great ministers and old generals were all suspicious, many rebelled and left, and Xian could not restrain it—thereby growing weaker.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was mild in manner but jealous at heart and could not bear rivals. Soon his senior ministers and veteran generals were estranged; many rebelled and left, and he could not stop them. His power dwindled from that point on.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔孝恭與李靖率巴蜀兵順流下，廬江王瑗繇襄陽道，黔州刺史田世康出辰州道，會兵圖銑。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict ordered Xiaogong and Li Jing to lead Ba-Shu troops downstream, Prince of Lujiang Yuan by the Xiangyang route, Prefect of Qian Zhou Tian Shikang by the Chenzhou route, joining forces to besiege Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year an edict sent Xiaogong and Li Jing down the Yangtze with the armies of Ba and Shu, the Prince of Lujiang Li Yuan along the Xiangyang road, and the prefect of Qianzhou Tian Shikang by the Chenzhou road, all to converge on Xian.

sentences.zh: 偽將周法明以四州降，即詔為黃州總管，趨夏口道，攻安州，克之。

translations.literal: The false general Zhou Faming with four prefectures surrendered; he was immediately appointed General-in-Chief of Huangzhou and hurried along the Xiakou route to attack Anzhou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: The false general Zhou Faming surrendered with four prefectures and was at once made General-in-Chief of Huangzhou. He pressed along the Xiakou route, attacked Anzhou, and took it.

sentences.zh: 偽將雷長潁以魯山降。

translations.literal: The false general Lei Changying with Lushan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The false general Lei Changying surrendered with Lushan.

sentences.zh: 銑乃遣將文士弘拒孝恭，戰清江口，孝恭大破之，獲鬥艦千艘，拔宜昌、當陽、枝江、松滋，偽江州將蓋彥舉以城降。

translations.literal: Xian then sent the general Wen Shihong to resist Xiaogong; they fought at Qingjiang mouth; Xiaogong greatly defeated him, captured a thousand war vessels, took Yichang, Dangyang, Zhijiang, Songzi; the false Jiangzhou general Gai Yan offered the city in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xian sent Wen Shihong to block Xiaogong. They fought at the mouth of the Qing River; Xiaogong won a crushing victory, seized a thousand warships, and took Yichang, Dangyang, Zhijiang, and Songzi. The false Jiangzhou general Gai Yan surrendered his city.

sentences.zh: 孝恭、靖直逼其都。

translations.literal: Xiaogong and Jing pressed directly on his capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong and Li Jing drove straight for his capital.

sentences.zh: 初，銑放兵，止留宿衛數千人，及倉卒追集，江、嶺回遠，未及赴。

translations.literal: Initially Xian had dismissed troops, retaining only several thousand palace guards; in haste when he mustered them, the Jiang and Ling regions were far—they could not arrive in time.
translations.idiomatic: Xian had earlier released his troops and kept only a few thousand palace guards. When he tried to rally them in haste, his armies in the distant Jiang and Ling regions could not reach him in time.

sentences.zh: 孝恭布長圍守之，數日，破其水城，取樓船數千。

translations.literal: Xiaogong deployed a long encirclement to besiege him; within several days he broke their water city and took several thousand tower ships.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong drew a long encirclement around the city. Within days he stormed their river fort and captured several thousand tower ships.

sentences.zh: 交州總管丘和、長史高士廉、司馬杜之松詣靖降。

translations.literal: The General-in-Chief of Jiaozhou Qiu He, Senior Recorder Gao Shilian, and Army Supervisor Du Zhisong went to Jing to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiaozhou commander Qiu He, senior recorder Gao Shilian, and army supervisor Du Zhisong came to Li Jing and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 銑度救不至，謂其下曰：「天不祚梁乎？

translations.literal: Xian judged rescue would not arrive and said to his followers: "Does Heaven not aid Liang?
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that relief would not come, Xian told his officers, "Has Heaven abandoned Liang?

sentences.zh: 待窮而下，必害百姓。

translations.literal: If we wait until exhausted before surrendering, the common people will surely be harmed.
translations.idiomatic: If we hold out until the end and only then yield, the people will surely suffer.

sentences.zh: 今城未拔，先出降，可免亂。

translations.literal: Now before the city is taken, if we first go out to surrender, disorder can be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: If we surrender before the walls fall, we may still spare them slaughter and chaos.

sentences.zh: 諸人何患無君？」

translations.literal: You people—what worry is there of lacking a lord?"
translations.idiomatic: As for you—will you lack a ruler to serve?"

sentences.zh: 乃麾而令，守陴者皆慟。

translations.literal: Thereupon he waved his hand and gave the order; those defending the walls all wept.
translations.idiomatic: He waved his hand and gave the command. Every man on the walls wept.

sentences.zh: 以太牢告於廟，率官屬緦衰布幘詣軍門，謝曰：「當死者銑爾，百姓非罪也，請無殺掠！」

translations.literal: With the great sacrificial beast he announced to the temple, led officials in hemp mourning and cloth headcloth to the army gate, apologizing: "The one who should die is Xian alone; the common people are not guilty—please do not kill and plunder!"
translations.idiomatic: He offered the great sacrifice in the ancestral temple, then led his officials in hemp mourning and plain headcloth to the enemy camp and said, "Let only Xian die. The people are innocent—please do not kill or plunder them!"

sentences.zh: 孝恭受之，護送京師。

translations.literal: Xiaogong received him and escorted him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong accepted his surrender and sent him to the capital under guard.

sentences.zh: 後數日，救兵至，且十余萬。

translations.literal: Several days later, relief troops arrived, more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later his relief armies arrived—more than a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 知銑降，乃送款。

translations.literal: Learning Xian had surrendered, they thereupon offered allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: When they learned Xian had submitted, they too offered their allegiance.

sentences.zh: 銑至，高祖讓之，對曰：「隋失其鹿，英雄競逐。

translations.literal: When Xian arrived, Emperor Gaozu rebuked him; he replied: "Sui lost the deer; heroes competed in the chase.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian was brought before Emperor Gaozu, the emperor reproached him. Xian answered, "Sui lost the empire, and heroes raced to seize it.

sentences.zh: 銑無天命，故為陛下禽，猶田橫南面，豈負漢哉？」

translations.literal: Xian lacked Heaven's mandate, therefore was captured by Your Majesty; it is like Tian Heng facing south—how would that burden Han?"
translations.idiomatic: I lacked Heaven's mandate, so Your Majesty took me captive. It is like Tian Heng still facing south as a king—how could that be a reproach to Han?"

sentences.zh: 帝怒其不屈，詔斬都市，年三十九。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry at his defiance; an edict beheaded him in the market; age thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged by his defiance and ordered him beheaded in the public market. He was thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 自僭國至滅凡五年。

translations.literal: From assuming the state to destruction altogether five years.
translations.idiomatic: From the day he claimed a kingdom until his fall, five years in all.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：銑，故梁子孫，起文吏，掩東南而有之，荊、楚好亂，氣俗然也。

translations.literal: The eulogizer says: Xian was a descendant of the former Liang, rose from a clerk, covered the southeast and possessed it—the Jing and Chu love disorder; custom and air are so.
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser writes: Xian was a scion of the old Liang who rose from the clerical ranks, seized the southeast, and held it. Jing and Chu have always loved turmoil; that is the temper of the place.

sentences.zh: 觀銑武雖不足，文有余矣，大抵盜仁義，詭世亂俗者，聖人所必誅。

translations.literal: Observing Xian, martial capacity though insufficient, civil wen surplus—by and large to steal benevolence and righteousness and deceive the age and disorder custom, such men the sages must punish.
translations.idiomatic: In martial force he was wanting, yet in rhetoric he was ample. Men who steal the names of benevolence and righteousness to mislead the age and stir custom are precisely those the sages condemn without mercy.

sentences.zh: 若銑力困計殫，以好言自釋於下，系虜在廷，抗辭不屈，偽辯易窮，卒以殊死，高祖聖矣哉！

translations.literal: As for when Xian's strength was exhausted and plans spent, using fine words to release himself to those below, bound captive at court yet defiant in speech—false argument easily exhausted, he ultimately died exceptionally; Emperor Gaozu was sage indeed!
translations.idiomatic: When his strength was spent and his schemes failed, he tried to win his men with fine words; brought bound into court, he still spoke defiantly. Hollow eloquence soon runs dry, and he died by the sword. In this Gaozu showed true sagacity.

sentences.zh: 輔公祏輔公祏，齊州臨濟人。

translations.literal: Fu Gongduo—Fu Gongduo was a man of Linji in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Fu Gongduo. Fu Gongduo was a native of Linji in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 隋季與鄉人杜伏威為盜，轉掠淮南。

translations.literal: In the Sui season he with his fellow townsman Du Fuwei became bandits, roving plunder in Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Sui he and his fellow townsman Du Fuwei turned bandit and ranged through Huainan, plundering as they went.

sentences.zh: 伏威兵浸盛，自號總管，以公祏為長史。

translations.literal: Fuwei's troops gradually prospered; he styled himself Commissioner-in-Chief and made Gongduo Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei's force grew steadily. He styled himself Commissioner-in-Chief and made Gongduo his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 賊李子通據江都，伏威使公祏以精卒數千度江擊之。

translations.literal: The bandit Li Zitong held Jiangdu; Fuwei sent Gongduo with several thousand elite soldiers to cross the river and strike him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Li Zitong held Jiangdu. Fuwei sent Gongduo with several thousand picked troops across the river to attack him.

sentences.zh: 子通拒戰，眾十倍，銳甚。

translations.literal: Zitong resisted in battle; his host was ten times greater and very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Zitong met them in battle with a force ten times larger and in high fighting trim.

sentences.zh: 公祏選甲士千人，操長刀居前，別以千人隨之，令曰：「卻者斬！」

translations.literal: Gongduo selected a thousand armored soldiers bearing long sabers to march in front, another thousand to follow, ordering: "Who retreats is beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Gongduo chose a thousand armored men with long sabers to lead the column and another thousand to follow behind, with the order: "Anyone who falls back will be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 公祏以眾殿。

translations.literal: Gongduo with the mass brought up the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Gongduo himself commanded the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 俄而子通方陣而進，長刀千人皆決死鬥，公祏縱左右翼搏之，子通大潰，降其眾數千。

translations.literal: Before long Zitong was advancing in square formation; the thousand long sabers all fought to the death; Gongduo unleashed the left and right wings to grapple them; Zitong was greatly routed and surrendered several thousand of his host.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zitong advanced in tight formation. The thousand sabermen fought as if they had no lives to lose. Gongduo threw in his left and right wings, and Zitong's army collapsed. Several thousand of his men surrendered.

sentences.zh: 伏威既遣使歸國，武德二年，詔授公祏淮南道行臺尚書左仆射，封舒國公。

translations.literal: After Fuwei had sent envoys to return to the state, in the second year of Wude an edict appointed Gongduo Left Vice-President of the Masters of Writing on the Huainan Circuit Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: After Fuwei had sent envoys to submit to the Tang court, in the second year of Wude an edict made Gongduo Left Vice-President of the Masters of Writing on the Huainan executive secretariat and enfeoffed him as Duke of Shu.

sentences.zh: 初，伏威與公祏少相愛，又兄事之，故軍中呼輔伯，尊禮略等。

translations.literal: Initially Fuwei and Gongduo loved each other in youth, and Fuwei also treated him as elder brother; therefore in the army they called him Elder Fu, respect nearly equal.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei and Gongduo had been close since youth, and Fuwei treated him as an elder brother. The army called him Elder Fu, and the honor shown him was nearly equal to Fuwei's own.

sentences.zh: 伏威稍忌之，乃署養子闞棱為左將軍，王雄誕為右將軍，推公祏為仆射，陰解其柄。

translations.literal: Fuwei gradually came to envy him; he then appointed his adoptive son Kan Ling as Left General, Wang Xiongdan as Right General, promoted Gongduo to Vice President, secretly divesting his authority.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei slowly grew jealous. He made his adopted son Kan Ling Left General and Wang Xiongdan Right General, raised Gongduo to Vice President in name, and quietly stripped him of real power.

sentences.zh: 公祏內怏怏不平，乃與故人左遊仙偽學辟谷以自晦。

translations.literal: Gongduo inwardly resentful and ill at ease, thereupon with his old friend Zuo Youxian pretended to study grain avoidance to conceal himself.
translations.idiomatic: Gongduo seethed inside. He and his old friend Zuo Youxian pretended to practice grain-avoidance dietetics so as to lie low.

sentences.zh: 六年，伏威入朝，留公祏居守，復令雄誕握兵副之，陰誡曰：「吾至京不失職，無容公祏為變。」

translations.literal: In the sixth year Fuwei entered court; he left Gongduo to guard, again ordered Wang Xiongdan to hold troops as deputy, secretly warning: "When I reach the capital I shall not lose office—you must not let Gongduo make trouble."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Fuwei went to court and left Gongduo behind as guardian. He again put Wang Xiongdan in command as his deputy and secretly warned him, "I shall keep my post in the capital—you must not let Gongduo stir up trouble."

sentences.zh: 後左遊仙說公祏反，會雄誕以疾臥家，公祏奪其兵，紿言伏威移書令舉事。

translations.literal: Later Zuo Youxian urged Gongduo to rebel; it happened Xiongdan lay ill at home; Gongduo seized his troops and deceived saying Fuwei had sent a letter ordering to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zuo Youxian talked Gongduo into rebellion. Xiongdan happened to be ill at home, and Gongduo seized his army, falsely claiming Fuwei had written ordering a rising.

sentences.zh: 八月，遂僭位，國稱宋，即陳故宮都之；

translations.literal: In the eighth month he presumptuously took the throne, the state titled Song, taking the former Chen palace as capital;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he declared himself emperor, named his state Song, and made his capital in the old Chen palace.

sentences.zh: 殺王雄誕，署百官，以左遊仙為兵部尚書、東南道大使、越州總管；

translations.literal: he killed Wang Xiongdan, appointed officials of all ranks, making Zuo Youxian Minister of War, Commissioner of the Southeastern Circuit, General-in-Chief of Yuezhou;
translations.idiomatic: He killed Wang Xiongdan, appointed officials at every rank, and made Zuo Youxian Minister of War, commissioner of the southeastern circuit, and general-in-chief of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 增修器械，轉廩食，遣將徐紹宗侵海州，陳正通寇壽陽。

translations.literal: he increased and repaired weapons, shifted granary grain, sent the general Xu Shaozong to invade Haizhou, Chen Zhengtong to raid Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: He expanded his armories, moved grain from the public granaries, and sent Xu Shaozong against Haizhou and Chen Zhengtong against Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 詔越郡王孝恭趨九江，嶺南大使李靖下宣城，懷州總管黃君漢出譙，齊州總管李世勣繇淮、泗討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Prince of Yue Xiaogong to hurry to Jiujiang, Grand Ambassador of Lingnan Li Jing down from Xuancheng, General-in-Chief of Huaizhou Huang Junhan out from Qiao, General-in-Chief of Qizhou Li Shiji by Huai and Si to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict sent the Prince of Yue Li Xiaogong to Jiujiang, the Lingnan envoy Li Jing down from Xuancheng, the Huai prefect Huang Junhan out of Qiao, and the Qi prefect Li Shiji up the Huai and Si to crush him.

sentences.zh: 孝恭取蕪湖，下梁山三鎮。

translations.literal: Xiaogong took Wuhu, descended on the three Liangshan forts.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong took Wuhu and reduced the three forts on Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 河南安撫大使任瑰拔揚子城，降偽將龍龕，遂據揚州。

translations.literal: The Henan Pacification Commissioner Ren Gui took Yangzi city, subdued the false general Long Kan, and thereupon occupied Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan pacification commissioner Ren Gui seized Yangzi and subdued the false general Long Kan, then held Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 公祏復遣將馮惠亮、陳當世屯博望山，陳正通、徐紹宗屯青州山以拒戰，孝恭率諸將破之，惠亮、正通走，李靖躡追百餘里，眾悉潰，正通等以五百騎奔丹陽。

translations.literal: Gongduo again sent the generals Feng Huiliang and Chen Dangshi to garrison Bowang mountain, Chen Zhengtong and Xu Shaozong to garrison Qingzhou mountain to resist battle; Xiaogong led the generals to defeat them; Huiliang and Zhengtong fled; Li Jing pursued more than a hundred li; the host entirely routed; Zhengtong and others with five hundred cavalry fled to Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gongduo sent Feng Huiliang and Chen Dangshi to hold Bowang Mountain and Chen Zhengtong and Xu Shaozong to hold Qingzhou Mountain. Xiaogong and his generals broke them; Huiliang and Zhengtong fled. Li Jing chased them more than a hundred li until their armies scattered. Zhengtong and the rest escaped to Danyang with five hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 公祏懼，棄城奔左遊仙於會稽，兵尚數萬。

translations.literal: Gongduo feared, abandoned the city and fled to Zuo Youxian at Kuaiji; troops still numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Gongduo panicked, abandoned his city, and fled to Zuo Youxian in Kuaiji. He still had tens of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 夜至毘陵，能從者裁五百。

translations.literal: At night he reached Piling; those who could follow barely five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Piling by night with barely five hundred followers.

sentences.zh: 偽將吳騷、孫安謀執之，公

translations.literal: The false generals Wu Sao and Sun An plotted to seize him; Gong
translations.idiomatic: The false generals Wu Sao and Sun An plotted to seize him. Fu

sentences.zh: 祏棄妻子斬關遁，與腹心士數十抵武康，野人執送丹陽，孝恭斬之，傳首京師擊李子通，始公祏佐伏威起據江東，距公祏死，凡十三年。

translations.literal: duo abandoned wife and children, cut through the pass and fled; with several dozen trusted followers he reached Wukang; rustic people seized and sent him to Danyang; Xiaogong beheaded him and sent the head to the capital to strike Li Zitong. From when Gongduo first aided Fuwei to rise and hold Jiangdong, until Gongduo's death, altogether thirteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Gongduo abandoned his wife and children, broke through the barrier, and fled. With a few dozen trusted men he reached Wukang, where country people seized him and delivered him to Danyang. Xiaogong beheaded him and sent the head to the capital as a warning when Li Zitong was attacked. From the day Gongduo helped Fuwei seize the lower Yangtze until his death, thirteen years had passed.

sentences.zh: 沈法興沈法興，湖州武康人。

translations.literal: Shen Faxing—Shen Faxing was a man of Wukang in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Shen Faxing. Shen Faxing was a native of Wukang in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 父恪，陳廣州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Ke was Inspector-General of Guangzhou under Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ke had been inspector-general of Guangzhou under Chen.

sentences.zh: 法興隋大業末為吳興郡守，東陽賊樓世幹略其郡，煬帝詔與太仆丞元祐討之。

translations.literal: Faxing at the end of Daye in Sui was Administrator of Wuxing commandery; the Dongyang bandit Lou Shigan raided his command; Emperor Yang ordered him with the Imperial Stud Vice Director Yuan You to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui, Faxing was administrator of Wuxing. The Dongyang rebel Lou Shigan raided his commandery, and Emperor Yang ordered Faxing, together with the imperial stud vice director Yuan You, to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 義寧二年，江都亂，法興自以世南土，屬姓數千家，遠近向服，乃與祐將孫士漢、陳果仁執祐，名誅宇文化及，三月發東陽，行收兵，趨江都，下余杭，比至烏程，眾六萬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yining, when Jiangdu was in chaos, Faxing considered himself of southern soil, his clan of the surname several thousand households, far and near oriented to him; he with You's general Sun Shihan and Chen Guoren seized You, nominally executing Yu Wen Huaji; in the third month he launched from Dongyang, marched gathering troops, hurried to Jiangdu, descended on Yuhang; by the time he reached Wucheng his host was sixty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yining, when Jiangdu fell into chaos, Faxing thought himself rooted in the south: his clan numbered thousands of households, and men far and near looked to him. With You's generals Sun Shihan and Chen Guoren he seized You, claiming to execute Yuwen Huaji. In the third month he marched from Dongyang, gathering troops as he went toward Jiangdu and down into Yuhang. By the time he reached Wucheng he had sixty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 毘陵通守路道德拒之，法興約連和，因襲殺之，據其城，遂定江表十余州，自署江南道總管。

translations.literal: The Piling Defender Lu Daode resisted him; Faxing proposed alliance and thus ambushed and killed him, occupied his city, thereupon settled more than ten prefectures of Jiangbiao, and on his own authority styled himself Commissioner of the Jiangnan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Piling defender Lu Daode barred his way. Faxing offered alliance, then ambushed and killed him, took his city, and soon controlled more than ten prefectures south of the Yangtze. He styled himself commissioner of the Jiangnan circuit on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 聞越王侗立，乃上書稱大司馬、錄尚書事、天門公，承制置百官，以陳果仁為司徒，孫士漢司空，蔣元超尚書左仆射，殷芊左丞，徐令言右丞，劉子翼選部侍郎，李百藥為掾。

translations.literal: Hearing that Prince of Yue Tong had been established, he thereupon sent a memorial styling himself Grand Marshal, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Duke of Tianmen, issuing edicts appointing officials—making Chen Guoren Minister of Education, Sun Shihan Minister of Works, Jiang Yuanchao Left Vice-President of the Masters of Writing, Yin Qian Left Assistant, Xu Lingyan Right Assistant, Liu Ziyi Selections Vice Director, Li Baiyao as clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Prince Yue Yang Tong had been set up at Luoyang, he sent a memorial styling himself grand marshal, recorder of the masters of writing, and Duke of Tianmen, and issued edicts appointing a full bureaucracy: Chen Guoren as minister of education, Sun Shihan as minister of works, Jiang Yuanchao as left vice-president of the masters of writing, Yin Qian as left assistant, Xu Lingyan as right assistant, Liu Ziyi as vice director of selections, and Li Baiyao as a secretarial officer.

sentences.zh: 後聞侗被廢，高祖武德二年，稱梁王，建元為延康，易隋官儀，頗用陳氏故事。

translations.literal: Later hearing Tong was deposed, in the second year of Wude of Emperor Gaozu he styled himself King of Liang, era name Yankang, changed Sui official ceremonies, largely using Chen precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he learned Tong had been deposed, in the second year of Wude he declared himself King of Liang, took the era name Yankang, and reshaped court ritual, drawing heavily on Chen practice.

sentences.zh: 法興自意南方諸城可跂而平，專事威戮，下有細過即誅之，繇是將士攜解。

translations.literal: Faxing himself thought the southern cities could be leveled at a stride; he devoted himself to stern killing—minor faults below and he executed; thereby generals and soldiers drifted apart.
translations.idiomatic: Faxing believed the southern cities would fall at a single step. He ruled by terror, executing men for the smallest fault, until his officers and soldiers lost heart.

sentences.zh: 俄遣子綸救陳棱，擊李子通，反為所敗。

translations.literal: Shortly he sent his son Lun to rescue Chen Cheng, attack Li Zitong, and was in turn defeated by him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he sent his son Lun to rescue Chen Cheng and attack Li Zitong, but Zitong defeated him in turn.

sentences.zh: 子通乘鋒度江，破京口。

translations.literal: Zitong riding the edge crossed the river and broke Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Zitong pressed his advantage across the river and stormed Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 使將蔣元超戰庱亭，大敗，死之。

translations.literal: He sent the general Jiang Yuanchao to fight at Chengting; greatly defeated; Yuanchao died.
translations.idiomatic: Faxing sent Jiang Yuanchao to fight at Chengting. Yuanchao was routed and killed.

sentences.zh: 法興懼，棄城與左右數百投吳郡賊聞人遂安，遂安遣將葉孝辯迎之。

translations.literal: Faxing feared, abandoned the city with several hundred followers and threw himself on the Wu Prefecture bandit Wen Ren Sui'an; Sui'an sent the general Ye Xiaobian to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: In fear Faxing abandoned his city and fled with a few hundred men to the Wu bandit Wen Ren Sui'an. Sui'an sent Ye Xiaobian to receive him.

sentences.zh: 法興中悔，將殺孝辯，趨會稽，為所覺，懼，自沈於江。

translations.literal: Faxing midway regretted, intending to kill Xiaobian and hurry to Kuaiji; he was discovered, feared, and drowned himself in the river.
translations.idiomatic: Halfway there Faxing changed his mind and meant to kill Xiaobian and push on to Kuaiji, but he was found out. In terror he threw himself into the river and drowned.

sentences.zh: 起義寧至武德，凡三年滅。

translations.literal: From rising in Yining to Wude, altogether three years until destruction.
translations.idiomatic: From his rising in Yining until his fall under Wude, three years in all.

sentences.zh: 李子通李子通，沂州承人。

translations.literal: Li Zitong—Li Zitong was a man of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Li Zitong. Li Zitong was a man of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 少貧，以漁獵為生。

translations.literal: In youth poor, he made a living by fishing and hunting.
translations.idiomatic: He was poor in his youth and lived by fishing and hunting.

sentences.zh: 居其鄉，見班白負戴，必代之，家有余，則以赒人，而喜報仇。

translations.literal: In his village, seeing gray-haired people carrying burdens he would always take their place; if the household had surplus he would aid others, and he delighted in avenging wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: In his home village, whenever he saw gray-haired elders carrying loads he would take the burden from them. If his family had a little extra he gave it away, and he loved to settle scores for others.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，長白山賊左才相自號博山公，子通依之，以武力雄其間。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye in Sui, the Changbai Mountain bandit Zuo Caixiang styled himself Duke of Boshan; Zitong attached to him, dominating the region by martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui, the Changbai Mountain bandit Zuo Caixiang styled himself Duke of Boshan. Zitong joined him and rose to the top of the band by sheer fighting strength.

sentences.zh: 鄉人有陷賊者，子通專經護之。

translations.literal: When fellow villagers were entrapped by bandits, Zitong would specially go protect them.
translations.idiomatic: When men from his village were caught up among the bandits, Zitong would go in person to shield them.

sentences.zh: 方是時，群盜暴忍，獨子通仁愛，歸者遂多，不半歲，有徒萬人。

translations.literal: At this time the bandits were cruel and violent; only Zitong was benevolent and humane, so those who came to him grew numerous; in less than half a year he had ten thousand followers.
translations.idiomatic: In those days the rebels were brutal, but Zitong alone showed kindness, and men flocked to him; within six months he commanded ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 才相畏忌，子通乃引眾度淮，與杜伏威合。

translations.literal: Zuocai feared and resented him, so Zitong led his host across the Huai to join Du Fuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Zuocai Xiang grew wary of him, and Zitong marched his forces south across the Huai to ally with Du Fuwei.

sentences.zh: 為隋將來整所破，奔海陵，得眾二萬，自稱將軍。

translations.literal: He was broken by the Sui general Lai Zheng, fled to Hailing, gathered twenty thousand men, and styled himself General.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated by the Sui commander Lai Zheng, he retreated to Hailing, raised twenty thousand troops, and proclaimed himself a general.

sentences.zh: 大業十一年僭號楚王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Daye he usurped the title King of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Daye he declared himself King of Chu.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及殺煬帝，以右禦衛將軍陳棱為江都太守，已而棱降，高祖授以總管，即守其郡。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji killed Emperor Yang, he appointed Right Imperial Guard General Chen Leng prefect of Jiangdu; later Chen Leng surrendered, and Gaozu appointed him regional commander, and he continued to hold the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuwen Huaji murdered Emperor Yang, he installed Chen Leng of the Right Imperial Guard as prefect of Jiangdu; Chen Leng soon submitted to Gaozu, who confirmed him as regional commander and left him in charge of the district.

sentences.zh: 子通攻棱，棱窮，乞師於沈法興、杜伏威。

translations.literal: Zitong attacked Chen Leng; Chen Leng was desperate and begged troops of Shen Faxing and Du Fuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Zitong besieged Chen Leng, who, hard pressed, appealed to Shen Faxing and Du Fuwei for relief.

sentences.zh: 伏威自將屯清流，法興遣子綸屯揚子，間數十里。

translations.literal: Fuwei led troops himself and camped at Qingliu; Faxing sent his son Lun to camp at Yangzi, only a few dozen li apart.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei marched in person and encamped at Qingliu, while Faxing posted his son Lun at Yangzi, their camps scarcely thirty li apart.

sentences.zh: 子通納言毛文深請募吳人詐為法興兵夜襲伏威，二人遂交惡，無敢先戰者。

translations.literal: Zitong's adviser Mao Wenshen proposed recruiting Wu men to feign being Faxing's troops and raid Fuwei by night; the two thus became hostile, and neither dared fight first.
translations.idiomatic: Zitong's counselor Mao Wenshen urged him to raise Wu men disguised as Faxing's army for a night attack on Fuwei; the two allies turned on each other, and neither would commit to battle.

sentences.zh: 子通得悉力取江都，遂據之，棱奔而免。

translations.literal: Zitong was thus able to bring his full strength against Jiangdu, seized it, and Chen Leng fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Free to concentrate his full strength on Jiangdu, Zitong took the city; Chen Leng broke out and escaped.

sentences.zh: 子通僭即皇帝位，國號吳，建元明政。

translations.literal: Zitong usurped the imperial throne; his state was called Wu and his reign era Mingzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zitong declared himself emperor of Wu, with the reign title Mingzheng.

sentences.zh: 齊賊樂伯通先為化及守丹陽，即以眾萬余降之，子通用為尚書左仆射。

translations.literal: The Qi bandit Yue Botong had first held Danyang for Huaji; he now surrendered with more than ten thousand men, and Zitong appointed him Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Botong of Qi, who had guarded Danyang for Yuwen Huaji, came over with ten thousand men; Zitong made him Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又敗法興兵，遂取晉陵，以法興所署掾李百藥為內史侍郎，典文檄，尚書左丞殷芊為太常卿，司禮樂，繇是江南士人多歸之。

translations.literal: He again defeated Faxing's army and took Jinling; he made Li Baiyao, whom Faxing had appointed as clerk, Vice Director of the Secretariat in charge of documents and proclamations, and Yin Qian, Left Assistant of the Imperial Secretariat, Director of Ceremonies in charge of ritual music; thereby many scholars of the Jiangnan region came to join him.
translations.idiomatic: After another victory over Shen Faxing he seized Jinling, installed Li Baiyao—once Faxing's clerk—as Vice Director of the Secretariat to draft state papers, and Yin Qian as Director of Ceremonies to oversee ritual music; learned men across the lower Yangtze flocked to his court.

sentences.zh: 會伏威命輔公祏拔丹陽，進屯溧水，子通戰敗，糧且盡，棄江都，保京口，伏威盡得其地。

translations.literal: When Fuwei ordered Fu Gongshi to take Danyang and advance to camp at Lishui, Zitong was defeated in battle, his provisions nearly exhausted; he abandoned Jiangdu and held Jingkou, while Fuwei took all his former territory.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei sent Fu Gongshi to seize Danyang and press on to Lishui; Zitong was beaten, his stores nearly gone, abandoned Jiangdu for Jingkou, and lost the rest of his domain to Fuwei.

sentences.zh: 俄東走太湖，裒散兵二萬人，復張，襲法興吳郡，破之。

translations.literal: Soon he fled east to Lake Tai, gathered scattered troops to twenty thousand, rose again, and raided Faxing's Wu commandery and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fled east to Lake Tai, rallied twenty thousand scattered soldiers, struck Shen Faxing's Wu commandery, and routed it.

sentences.zh: 據余杭。

translations.literal: He held Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: He occupied Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 東舉會稽，南距嶺，西抵宣城，北太湖，悉有之。

translations.literal: East to Kuaiji, south to the Ling region, west to Xuancheng, north to Lake Tai — he held them all.
translations.idiomatic: His sway ran east to Kuaiji, south to the mountain passes, west to Xuancheng, and north to Lake Tai.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，伏威遣將王雄誕討子通。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, Fuwei sent the general Wang Xiongqian to attack Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Wude, Du Fuwei dispatched Wang Xiongqian against Li Zitong.

sentences.zh: 戰蘇州，敗績，退保余杭，雄誕進傅城。

translations.literal: They fought at Suzhou; Zitong was defeated, retreated to hold Yuhang, and Xiongqian advanced to besiege the city.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated at Suzhou, Zitong fell back on Yuhang while Xiongqian laid siege.

sentences.zh: 子通窮。

translations.literal: Zitong was desperate.
translations.idiomatic: Zitong was at his wit's end.

sentences.zh: 乃降，伏威受之，並樂伯通送京師。

translations.literal: He then surrendered; Fuwei accepted it and sent both him and Yue Botong to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He surrendered; Fuwei received him and sent him and Yue Botong to the capital.

sentences.zh: 高祖薄其罪，賜宅一區、田五頃，賚予頗厚。

translations.literal: Gaozu judged his crime lightly, granted him one residence and five qing of land, and gave him generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu treated his offense leniently, granted a house and five qing of fields, and rewarded him handsomely.

sentences.zh: 及伏威來朝，子通語伯通曰：「東南未靖，而伏威來。

translations.literal: When Fuwei came to court, Zitong said to Botong: "The southeast is not yet pacified, yet Fuwei has come to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Fuwei went to court, Zitong told Botong, "The southeast is still unsettled, yet Fuwei has left for the capital.

sentences.zh: 我故兵多在江外，若收之，可建大功。」

translations.literal: Many of my old soldiers remain beyond the river; if we gather them, we can achieve great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Most of our old troops are still south of the river; rally them and we can win glory again.

sentences.zh: 遂皆亡。

translations.literal: They both fled.
translations.idiomatic: Both men fled.

sentences.zh: 及藍田，為關吏所獲，並伏誅。

translations.literal: At Lantian they were seized by frontier officials and both were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Near Lantian the frontier guards seized them, and both were put to death.

sentences.zh: 方子通等僭盛時，復有硃粲、林士弘、張善安亦竊名號於淮、楚間。

translations.literal: About when Zitong and others were at their height in usurpation, Zhu Can, Lin Shihong, and Zhang Shian also seized titles in the Huai and Chu regions.
translations.idiomatic: While Zitong and his peers were at their peak, Zhu Can, Lin Shihong, and Zhang Shian also carved out titles between the Huai and the Chu country.

sentences.zh: 朱粲朱粲，亳州城父人。

translations.literal: Zhu Can — Zhu Can was a native of Chengyi in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Can was born in Chengyi, Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 初為縣史。

translations.literal: He was first a county clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a county clerk.

sentences.zh: 大業中從軍，伐賊長白山，亡命去為盜，號「可達寒賊」，自稱迦樓羅王，眾十萬。

translations.literal: During Daye he joined the army against the bandits of Changbai Mountain, fled and became a bandit, styled himself the "Kedahan Bandit" and King Garuda, with one hundred thousand followers.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye era he served in the campaign against the Changbai rebels, then deserted, styled himself the Kedahan Bandit and King Garuda, and gathered a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 度淮屠景陵、沔陽，轉剽山南，所至殘戮無遺噍。

translations.literal: He crossed the Huai, slaughtered Jingling and Mianyang, and turned to raid south of the mountains, leaving nothing alive wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Huai he sacked Jingling and Mianyang, then swept through the southern hills, slaughtering every place he touched.

sentences.zh: 僭號楚帝，建元為昌達。

translations.literal: He usurped the title Emperor of Chu and adopted the reign era Changda.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed himself Emperor of Chu with the era name Changda.

sentences.zh: 攻拔南陽。

translations.literal: He attacked and took Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 義寧末，與山南撫慰使馬元規戰冠軍，大敗，收余眾，復振，至二十萬。

translations.literal: At the end of Yining he fought the Shannan pacification commissioner Ma Yuangui at Guanjun and was badly defeated; he gathered his remnants, rose again, and reached two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Yining period he met Ma Yuangui, the Shannan pacifier, at Guanjun and was shattered; rallying his survivors he swelled again to two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 粲所克州縣皆發藏粟以食，遷徙無常，去輒燔廥聚，毀城郭，不務稼穡，專以劫為資。

translations.literal: In every prefecture and county he took, Can opened stored grain to feed his men; he moved without fixed abode, and on leaving always burned granaries and destroyed walls, cared nothing for farming, and relied solely on plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he conquered he emptied the granaries to feed his troops, never staying long: on departure he burned storehouses, wrecked walls, ignored agriculture, and lived by raiding alone.

sentences.zh: 於是人大餒，死者系路，其軍亦匱，乃掠小兒蒸食之。

translations.literal: The people starved severely, the dead lined the roads, his army too was exhausted, and he began seizing children and steaming them for food.
translations.idiomatic: Famine stalked the land and corpses choked the roads; his own army ran dry, and he began kidnapping children to steam for rations.

sentences.zh: 戒其徒曰：「味之珍寧有加人者？

translations.literal: He warned his followers: "Is there any delicacy greater than human flesh?
translations.idiomatic: He told his men, "What delicacy surpasses human flesh?

sentences.zh: 弟使佗國有人，我恤無儲哉！」

translations.literal: Only let other lands have people — why should I worry about stores!
translations.idiomatic: So long as other states still have people, why should I fret over provisions!

sentences.zh: 勒所部略婦人孺兒分烹之，又稅諸城細弱以益糧。

translations.literal: He ordered his troops to seize women and children, divide and cook them, and also levied the weak from every city to augment provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He forced his troops to seize women and children for communal cooking and taxed the frail in every town to swell his larder.

sentences.zh: 隋著作佐郎陸從典、通事舍人顏湣楚謫南陽，粲初引為賓客，後盡食兩家。

translations.literal: The Sui Adjunct Author-editor Lu Congdian and Palace Herald Yan Mintu, exiled to Nanyang, were first invited as guests by Can and later his troops devoured both households entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congdian, a Sui adjunct in the Author's Bureau, and Yan Mintu, a Palace Herald, both exiled to Nanyang, were welcomed as guests—then his soldiers devoured both families to the last.

sentences.zh: 俄而諸城懼，皆逃散。

translations.literal: Soon every city was terrified and all fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Terror spread through the towns, and the populace fled.

sentences.zh: 顯州首領楊士林、田瓚起兵攻粲，旁郡響赴，戰淮源，粲大敗，挈殘士奔菊潭，遣使乞降。

translations.literal: Xianzhou leaders Yang Silin and Tian Zan raised troops against Can; neighboring commanderies responded; at Huaiyuan Can was greatly defeated, fled with his remnants to Jutan, and sent envoys to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Silin and Tian Zan of Xianzhou rose against him; neighboring districts joined in; defeated at Huaiyuan, Can fled with his survivors to Jutan and sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 高祖以前御史大夫段確假散騎常侍勞之。

translations.literal: Gaozu appointed the former Censor-in-chief Duan Que acting Regular Attendant to console him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent the former Censor-in-chief Duan Que, acting as Regular Attendant, to accept his submission.

sentences.zh: 確醉，戲粲曰：「君膾人多矣，若為味？」

translations.literal: Que was drunk and jested with Can: "You have minced many people — how does the taste compare?
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, Duan joked, "You have butchered so many—how do they taste?

sentences.zh: 粲曰：「啖嗜酒人，正似糟豚。」

translations.literal: Can said: "Eating a wine-lover is just like pickled pork."
translations.idiomatic: Can replied, "A drunkard is rather like pickled pork."

sentences.zh: 確悸，罵曰：「狂賊，歸朝乃一奴耳，復得噬人乎？」

translations.literal: Que was alarmed and cursed: "Mad bandit — once you submit to the court you are but a slave; can you still devour men?"
translations.idiomatic: Duan, shaken, cursed him: "Mad rebel! In the capital you are only a bondsman—would you dare eat men again?"

sentences.zh: 粲懼，收確於坐，並從者數十悉饔之，以饗左右。

translations.literal: Can was afraid; he seized Que at the banquet and with several dozen attendants fed them all to his men to feast his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Can seized Duan at the feast and, with several dozen of his escort, cooked them all to regale his officers.

sentences.zh: 遂屠菊潭，奔王世充，署龍驤大將軍。

translations.literal: He then slaughtered Jutan, fled to Wang Shichong, and was appointed Dragon-Flying Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He massacred Jutan, fled to Wang Shichong, and was named Dragon-Flying Grand General.

sentences.zh: 東都平，斬洛水上。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, he was beheaded on the Luo River.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern capital fell, he was executed on the banks of the Luo.

sentences.zh: 士庶競擲瓦礫擊其屍，須臾若冢。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners vied to hurl stones and tiles at his corpse until in a moment it was like a mound.
translations.idiomatic: Citizens pelted his body with brick and stone until it rose like a barrow.

sentences.zh: 林士弘林士弘，饒州鄱陽人。

translations.literal: Lin Shihong — Lin Shihong was a native of Poyang in Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Shihong came from Poyang in Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 隋季與鄉人操師乞起為盜。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui he and a fellow townsman Cao Shiji rose as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Sui he and a townsman, Cao Shiji, turned bandit.

sentences.zh: 師乞自號元興王，建元天成，大業十二年據豫章，以士弘為大將軍。

translations.literal: Shiji styled himself King Yuanxing, era Tiancheng; in the twelfth year of Daye he held Yuzhang and made Shihong Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji called himself King Yuanxing with the era Tiancheng; in the twelfth year of Daye he seized Yuzhang and made Shihong his Grand General.

sentences.zh: 隋遣治書侍御史劉子翊討賊，射殺師乞，而士弘收其眾，復戰彭蠡，子翊敗，死之。

translations.literal: The Sui sent Investigative Censor Liu Ziyi to suppress the bandits; he shot and killed Shiji, but Shihong gathered his forces, fought again at Poyang Lake, and Ziyi was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Investigative Censor Liu Ziyi, who killed Shiji in battle; Shihong rallied the remnant, met Liu again on Poyang Lake, and slew him.

sentences.zh: 遂大振，眾十余萬，據虔州，自號南越王。

translations.literal: He flourished greatly with more than one hundred thousand men, held Qianzhou, and styled himself King of Southern Yue.
translations.idiomatic: His power surged past a hundred thousand; he held Qianzhou and styled himself King of Southern Yue.

sentences.zh: 俄僭號楚：稱皇帝，建元為太平。

translations.literal: Soon he usurped the state of Chu, proclaimed himself emperor, and adopted the reign era Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: He soon declared the Chu dynasty, took the imperial title, and adopted the era Taiping.

sentences.zh: 侍御史鄭大節以九江郡下之。

translations.literal: Censor Attendant Zheng Dajie surrendered Jiujiang commandery to him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Attendant Zheng Dajie delivered Jiujiang to him.

sentences.zh: 士弘任其黨王戎為司空。

translations.literal: Shihong appointed his follower Wang Rong Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Shihong named his partisan Wang Rong Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 臨川、廬陵、南康、宜春豪傑皆殺隋守令以附，北盡九江，南番禺，悉有之。

translations.literal: Notables of Linchuan, Luling, Nankang, and Yichun all killed Sui prefects and magistrates to join him; north to Jiujiang, south to Panyu — he held them all.
translations.idiomatic: Local strongmen in Linchuan, Luling, Nankang, and Yichun killed Sui officials to join him; his realm stretched from Jiujiang north to Panyu south.

sentences.zh: 後蕭銑以舟師破豫章，士弘獨有南昌、虔、循、潮之地。

translations.literal: Later Xiao Xian's fleet took Yuzhang; Shihong alone retained Nanchang, Qian, Xun, and Chao.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Xian's fleet seized Yuzhang, Shihong kept only Nanchang, Qian, Xun, and Chao.

sentences.zh: 銑敗，其亡卒稍歸之，復振。

translations.literal: When Xian was defeated, his scattered soldiers gradually returned to Shihong, and he revived.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiao Xian's fall his fugitives drifted back, and Shihong revived.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王孝恭招慰，降循、潮二州。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao-jun Xiaogong offered pacification and received the surrender of Xun and Chao commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiaogong of Zhao offered terms and won Xun and Chao.

sentences.zh: 武德五年，士弘弟鄱陽王藥師以兵二萬圍循州，總管楊世略破斬之，士弘請降。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wude, Shihong's brother the Prince of Poyang Yaoshi besieged Xunzhou with twenty thousand men; regional commander Yang Shilue defeated and killed him, and Shihong requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Wude his brother Yaoshi, Prince of Poyang, invested Xunzhou with twenty thousand men; Yang Shilue destroyed the force and killed him, and Shihong sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 王戎亦獻南昌地，詔戎為南昌州總管。

translations.literal: Wang Rong also offered Nanchang territory; an edict made Rong regional commander of Nanchang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong yielded Nanchang as well; the court made him regional commander of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 士弘復遁保安城山，誘潰亡，謀復亂，袁人相聚應之，為張善安所察，以兵赴討。

translations.literal: Shihong again fled to Bao'an Chengcheng Mountain, rallied stragglers, plotted renewed rebellion; Yuan men gathered in response; Zhang Shian detected it and marched troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Shihong slipped to Bao'an Chengcheng Mountain, gathered deserters, and plotted a comeback; Yuanzhou men answered his call, but Zhang Shian uncovered the scheme and marched against him.

sentences.zh: 會士弘死，其黨乃解。

translations.literal: When Shihong died, his faction dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Shihong died before the plot matured, and his party dissolved.

sentences.zh: 張善安張善安，兗州方與人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shian — Zhang Shian was a native of Fangyu in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shian was from Fangyu in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 年十七，亡命為盜，轉掠淮南。

translations.literal: At seventeen he fled as outlaw and became a bandit, raiding through Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he became an outlaw and roamed Huainan as a bandit.

sentences.zh: 會孟讓敗，得其散卒八百，襲破廬江郡。

translations.literal: When Meng Rang was defeated he got eight hundred of his scattered troops and raided and took Lujiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Meng Rang's defeat he picked up eight hundred survivors and stormed Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 依林士弘，不見信，憾之，反襲士弘，焚其郛，去保南康。

translations.literal: He attached to Lin Shihong but was not trusted, resented it, turned and raided Shihong, burned his outer walls, and withdrew to hold Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Lin Shihong without trust, he turned on him, burned his outer ramparts, and withdrew to Nankang.

sentences.zh: 蕭銑取豫章，遣將蘇胡兒守之，善安奪其地，據以歸國，授洪州總管。

translations.literal: Xiao Xian took Yuzhang and sent Su Hu'er to hold it; Shian seized the territory, submitted to the state, and was appointed regional commander of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Xian seized Yuzhang he left Su Hu'er to guard it; Shian drove him out, submitted to Tang, and was made regional commander of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 武德六年反，輔公祏以為西南道大行臺。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wude he rebelled; Fu Gongshi made him Grand Commander of the Southwest Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Wude he rebelled; Fu Gongshi named him Grand Commander of the Southwest Circuit.

sentences.zh: 善安掠孫州，執總管王戎，襲殺黃州總管周法明。

translations.literal: Shian raided Sun prefecture, seized regional commander Wang Rong, and ambushed and killed Huangzhou commander Zhou Faming.
translations.idiomatic: He plundered Sunzhou, seized Wang Rong, and killed Huangzhou commander Zhou Faming in an ambush.

sentences.zh: 會李大亮兵至，為開曉禍福，答曰：「善安初不反，為部下詿誤。

translations.literal: When Li Daliang's troops arrived, he explained the consequences of fortune and misfortune; Shian answered: "Shian did not rebel at first; my subordinates misled me.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daliang arrived and explained the stakes; Shian said, "I never meant to rebel—my officers misled me.

sentences.zh: 降，今易耳，恐不免，奈何？」

translations.literal: To surrender now is easy, but I fear I cannot escape — what can be done?
translations.idiomatic: Surrender is easy now, yet I fear I may not be spared—what am I to do?

sentences.zh: 大亮曰：「總管定降，吾固不疑。」

translations.literal: Daliang said: "Commander, you have decided to surrender; I never doubted it."
translations.idiomatic: Daliang said, "If you mean to submit, I never doubted you."

sentences.zh: 因獨入其陣，與善安握手語，乃大喜，將數十騎詣大亮營。

translations.literal: He then entered Shian's lines alone, spoke hand in hand with him; Shian was greatly pleased and came with several dozen riders to Daliang's camp.
translations.idiomatic: He rode alone into Shian's ranks, clasped his hand in talk, and Shian, delighted, followed with a few dozen horsemen to Daliang's camp.

sentences.zh: 大亮引入，命壯士執之。

translations.literal: Daliang led him in and ordered stalwarts to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang ushered him inside and had braves seize him.

sentences.zh: 騎皆驚，引去，悉兵來戰。

translations.literal: The riders were alarmed, withdrew, and brought their full force to battle.
translations.idiomatic: His escort fled in alarm and returned with the whole army to fight.

sentences.zh: 大亮諭以善安自歸，無庸鬥。

translations.literal: Daliang announced that Shian had surrendered of his own accord and there was no need to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang proclaimed that Shian had come over willingly and that battle was needless.

sentences.zh: 其黨罵曰：「總管賣我！」

translations.literal: His followers cursed: "The commander has sold us out!
translations.idiomatic: His men shouted, "Our commander has sold us!

sentences.zh: 遂潰。

translations.literal: They then scattered.
translations.idiomatic: They broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 送善安京師，稱不與公祏謀，高祖赦之。

translations.literal: Shian was sent to the capital; he claimed he had not plotted with Gongshi; Gaozu pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Shian was sent to the capital, swore he had not conspired with Fu Gongshi, and Gaozu pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 公祏破，得其書，遂伏誅。

translations.literal: When Gongshi was defeated, his correspondence was found and Shian was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongshi fell, letters implicating Shian surfaced, and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 梁師都梁師都，夏州朔方人。

translations.literal: Liang Shidu — Liang Shidu was a native of Shuofang in Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shidu was a man of Shuofang in Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 為郡豪姓。

translations.literal: He was of a great clan of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His family was a leading house of the district.

sentences.zh: 仕隋鷹揚府郎將。

translations.literal: He served Sui as a commandant of the Hawk-raiser Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he held a captaincy in the Hawk-raiser Guard.

sentences.zh: 大業末罷歸，結徒起為盜，殺郡丞唐世宗，據郡稱大丞相，聯兵突厥。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he was dismissed and returned home, gathered followers and rose as bandits, killed Assistant Prefect Tang Shizong, held the commandery and styled himself Grand Chancellor, and allied with the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed late in Daye, he returned home, raised a band, killed Assistant Prefect Tang Shizong, seized the commandery as Grand Chancellor, and allied with the Turks.

sentences.zh: 與隋將張世隆戰，敗之，因略定雕陰、弘化、延安。

translations.literal: He fought the Sui general Zhang Shilong, defeated him, and thereby overran Diaoyin, Honghua, and Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the Sui general Zhang Shilong and overran Diaoyin, Honghua, and Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 自為梁國，僭皇帝位，祭天於城南，坎地瘞玉得印，以為瑞，建元永隆。

translations.literal: He made himself the state of Liang, usurped the imperial title, sacrificed to Heaven south of the city; digging the earth to bury jade he obtained a seal and took it as an omen; reign era Yonglong.
translations.idiomatic: He declared the Liang state, took the imperial title, and sacrificed to Heaven south of the city; burying jade in a pit he unearthed a seal and hailed it as a portent, adopting the era Yonglong.

sentences.zh: 始畢可汗遺以狼頭纛，號大度毘伽可汗、解事天子，遂導突厥兵居河南地，拔鹽川郡。

translations.literal: Qibi Khan sent him a wolf-head banner, titled him Great Khan Dubi Qaghan and "Understanding Heaven Son"; he then guided Turk troops to settle south of the Yellow River and took Yanchuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Qibi Khan gave him a wolf-head standard and named him Great Khan Dubi Qaghan, "Heaven-Solving Son of Heaven"; he led Turk forces into the Ordos and seized Yanchuan.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，寇靈州，長史楊則擊走之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude he raided Lingzhou; Chief Administrator Yang Ze repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wude he raided Lingzhou; Chief Administrator Yang Ze drove him off.

sentences.zh: 又與突厥千騎營野豬嶺，延州總管段德操勒兵不戰，師都氣懈，遣兵進擊，戰酣，德操自以輕騎出其旁乘之，師都大潰，逐北二百里，俘馘甚眾。

translations.literal: Again with a thousand Turk cavalry he camped at Wild Boar Ridge; Yan'an regional commander Duan Decao held his troops without fighting until Shidu's spirit flagged, then sent troops to attack; mid-battle Decao himself led light cavalry to strike from the flank; Shidu was routed utterly; they pursued north two hundred li and took many captives and heads.
translations.idiomatic: Again he camped at Wild Boar Ridge with a thousand Turk horsemen; Duan Decao of Yanzhou held back until Shidu's men slackened, then struck; as the fight peaked Decao swept in with light cavalry from the flank, shattered Shidu, pursued two hundred li north, and took a vast toll of captives and heads.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以步騎五千入寇，德操又盡屠其軍，降堡將張舉、劉旻。

translations.literal: Before long he invaded with five thousand foot and horse; Decao again annihilated his army and received the surrender of fortress generals Zhang Ju and Liu Min.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned with five thousand infantry and cavalry; Decao annihilated the force and accepted the surrender of fortress commanders Zhang Ju and Liu Min.

sentences.zh: 師都懼，遣尚書陸季覽說處羅可汗曰：「隋亡，中國裂為四五，勢均力弱，皆爭附突厥。

translations.literal: Shidu was afraid and sent Minister Lu Jilan to persuade Qulü Qaghan: "Sui is dead; China is split into four or five parts, equal in strength and weak, each competing to attach to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing ruin, Shidu sent Minister Lu Jilan to Qulü Qaghan: "Sui is gone; China is broken into four or five weak rivals, each courting the Turks.

sentences.zh: 今唐滅劉武周，國益大，兵方四出。

translations.literal: Now Tang has destroyed Liu Wuzhou; the state grows greater and armies march in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: Tang has just destroyed Liu Wuzhou and grows stronger by the day, sending armies in every direction.

sentences.zh: 師都將朝夕亡，然次亦及突厥，願可汁如魏孝文，兵引而南，師都請為鄉道。」

translations.literal: Shidu will perish any day, yet next it will reach the Turks as well. May the Qaghan, like Emperor Xiaowen of Wei, lead your army south — Shidu asks to serve as guide.
translations.idiomatic: I shall fall soon, but you will be next. I beg the Qaghan, as Emperor Xiaowen of Wei once did, to march south—I will guide your way.

sentences.zh: 處羅納之，令莫賀咄設入五原，泥步設與師都趨延州，處羅自攻太原，突利可汗與奚、霫、契丹、靺羯繇幽州道合，竇建德自滏口會晉、絳。

translations.literal: Qulü accepted; ordered Moheduo She into Wuyuan, Nibu She with Shidu toward Yanzhou, Qulü himself to attack Taiyuan, Tuli Qaghan with Xi, Mohe, Khitan, and Malgal by the Youzhou route to join, Dou Jiande from Fukou to meet at Jin and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qulü agreed: Moheduo She would enter Wuyuan, Nibu She advance with Shidu on Yanzhou, Qulü strike Taiyuan, Tuli Qaghan lead Xi, Mohe, Khitan, and Malgal down the Youzhou road, and Dou Jiande march from Fukou toward Jin and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 已而處羅死，兵不出，又為德操所破。

translations.literal: Soon Qulü died, the armies did not march out, and Shidu was again defeated by Decao.
translations.idiomatic: Qulü died before the armies moved; Shidu was beaten again by Decao.

sentences.zh: 六年，其將賀遂、索周以所部十二州降。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, his generals He Sui and Suo Zhou surrendered twelve commanderies with their troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year his generals He Sui and Suo Zhou surrendered twelve prefectures with their forces.

sentences.zh: 德操悉兵攻之，拔東城，師都保西城不敢出，求救於突厥頡利，頡利以勁兵萬騎赴之。

translations.literal: Decao brought his full force; took the eastern city; Shidu held the western city and dared not emerge, begging aid from Turk Ilü Qaghan, who came with ten thousand crack horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Decao attacked in full strength, took the eastern city, and penned Shidu in the western citadel; Shidu begged Ilü Qaghan, who came with ten thousand elite horsemen.

sentences.zh: 先是，稽胡大帥劉屳成以眾附師都，因讒見殺，其下疑懼，乃多叛。

translations.literal: Earlier the Jiihu chieftain Liu Shancheng had attached his forces to Shidu; through slander he was killed; his men grew suspicious and fearful, and many rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Jiihu leader Liu Shancheng had joined him; slandered, he was executed, and his followers, fearful, deserted in droves.

sentences.zh: 師都日益蹙，遂往朝頡利，教使南略，故突厥盜邊無寧歲，遂窺渭橋。

translations.literal: Shidu grew daily more pressed, went in person to court Ilü, and urged southern raids; thus Turk border raids knew no peaceful year until they eyed Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Growing desperate, Shidu went to court Ilü in person and urged raids south; Turk incursions plagued the frontier for years until they probed Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 後突厥政亂，太宗以師都浸危，乃諭以書使歸，不從。

translations.literal: Later when Turk politics fell into disorder, Taizong judged Shidu increasingly desperate and sent letters urging surrender; he would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: When Turk politics later collapsed, Taizong saw Shidu weakening and wrote urging submission; he refused.

sentences.zh: 詔夏州長史劍旻、司馬劍蘭經略之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Xiazhou Chief Administrator Jian Min and Vice Prefect Jian Lan to manage the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Xiazhou Chief Administrator Jian Min and Vice Prefect Jian Lan to conduct the campaign.

sentences.zh: 獲生口，縱以為間，君臣離撓。

translations.literal: Captives were taken and released to sow discord; lord and ministers were estranged.
translations.idiomatic: They took prisoners and released them as agents of discord until lord and ministers split.

sentences.zh: 出輕騎蹂其稼，城中饑虛。

translations.literal: Light cavalry trampled his crops; the city grew hungry and empty.
translations.idiomatic: Light horsemen trampled his fields, and hunger emptied the city.

sentences.zh: 又天狗墮其城。

translations.literal: Again a "heavenly dog" fell upon his city.
translations.idiomatic: A "heavenly dog" omen struck the walls as well.

sentences.zh: 辛獠兒、李正寶、馮端皆其健將，謀執師都降，不果，正寶挺身歸。

translations.literal: Xin Laor, Li Zhengbao, and Feng Duan were all his able generals; they plotted to seize Shidu and surrender but failed; Zhengbao alone fled to submit.
translations.idiomatic: His best generals—Xin Laor, Li Zhengbao, and Feng Duan—plotted to seize him and surrender; the plot failed, but Zhengbao escaped to the Tang alone.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，旻、蘭表可取狀，詔柴紹、薛萬均並力，令旻以勁卒直據朔方東城。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan, Min and Lan memorialized that he could be taken; an edict ordered Chai Shao and Xue Wanjun to combine forces and Min to lead crack troops straight to hold Shuofang's eastern city.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenguan, Min and Lan reported him ripe for conquest; Chai Shao and Xue Wanjun were ordered to unite, with Min's picked troops to seize Shuofang's eastern city.

sentences.zh: 頡利來援，會大雪，羊馬死，紹逆戰，破之，進屯城下。

translations.literal: Ilü came to aid; heavy snow fell and sheep and horses perished; Shao met them in battle, broke them, and advanced to camp below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Ilü marched to relieve the siege, but blizzards killed his herds; Chai Shao met and routed him, then encamped beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 其從父弟洛仁斬師都降，擢洛仁為右驍衛將軍、朔方郡公。

translations.literal: His paternal cousin Luoren killed Shidu and surrendered; Luoren was promoted to General of the Right Swift-Cavalry Guard and Duke of Shuofang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Luoren slew Shidu and submitted; Luoren was made General of the Right Swift-Cavalry Guard and Duke of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 自起至滅十二年。

translations.literal: From rise to destruction, twelve years.
translations.idiomatic: From his rise to his fall was twelve years.

sentences.zh: 以其地為夏州。

translations.literal: His territory was made Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: His lands were reorganized as Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 始師都據郡時，劉季真、郭子和者亦俱起，子和自有傳。

translations.literal: When Shidu first held the commandery, Liu Jizhen and Guo Zihe also rose; Zihe has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: When Shidu first seized the commandery, Liu Jizhen and Guo Zihe had also risen; Zihe has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 劉季真劉季真，離石胡人。

translations.literal: Liu Jizhen — Liu Jizhen was a Hu man of Lishi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jizhen was a Hu of Lishi.

sentences.zh: 父龍兒，大業十年舉兵自稱王，以季真為太子，弟六兒為永安王。

translations.literal: His father Long'er in the tenth year of Daye raised troops and styled himself king, made Jizhen crown prince and his brother Liu'er Prince of Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Long'er rebelled in the tenth year of Daye, crowned himself king, made Jizhen crown prince, and his younger brother Liu'er Prince of Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 鋒甚銳，將軍潘長文連年擊，不能下。

translations.literal: Their edge was very sharp; General Pan Changwen attacked for years without reducing them.
translations.idiomatic: Their raids were fierce; General Pan Changwen campaigned for years without breaking them.

sentences.zh: 後虎賁郎將梁德破殺龍兒，眾乃散。

translations.literal: Later Tiger Guard commandant Liang De defeated and killed Long'er and the host dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger Guard commandant Liang De finally killed Long'er and the band scattered.

sentences.zh: 唐兵起，六兒復聚為盜，附劉武周，季真從之，自號太子王，六兒為拓定王，叠為邊害。

translations.literal: When Tang armies rose, Liu'er again gathered as bandits, attached to Liu Wuzhou, and Jizhen followed; he styled himself King of the Crown Prince and Liu'er King of Tuoding; they piled border harms one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang rose, Liu'er banded together again under Liu Wuzhou; Jizhen followed, styling himself King of the Crown Prince while Liu'er became King of Tuoding, and together they ravaged the frontier.

sentences.zh: 西河公張綸、真鄉公李仲文合兵討之，季真降，詔以為石州總管，賜姓李，封彭山郡王。

translations.literal: Duke of Xihe Zhang Lun and Duke of Zhenxiang Li Zhongwen combined forces against them; Jizhen surrendered; an edict made him regional commander of Shizhou, granted the surname Li, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Pengshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lun, Duke of Xihe, and Li Zhongwen, Duke of Zhenxiang, jointly suppressed them; Jizhen submitted, was made regional commander of Shizhou, granted the surname Li, and enfeoffed as Prince of Pengshan.

sentences.zh: 宋金剛戰澮州，勢未決，遂復連武周。

translations.literal: At the battle of Fenzhou with Song Jingang the outcome was still unsettled, so he again linked with Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: While Song Jingang fought at Fenzhou with the issue still in doubt, he rejoined Liu Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 及敗，秦王執六兒斬之，季真奔高滿政，俄被殺。

translations.literal: When defeated, the Prince of Qin seized Liu'er and beheaded him; Jizhen fled to Gao Manzheng and was soon killed.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat the Prince of Qin captured Liu'er and beheaded him; Jizhen fled to Gao Manzheng and was killed soon after.
